# Job 5 — Group 02A staged explanation revisions

## Q1 — key A

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Therapeutic response patient ke actual emotion ko acknowledge karti hai. Yahan disappointment ke saath misunderstood feel karna main concern hai. Nurse feeling reflect karke open-ended question se patient ko apni priority explain karne ka chance deti hai. Acceptance ka matlab har belief se agree karna nahi, balki patient ke experience ko respect karna hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A emotion acknowledge karta hai aur further discussion invite karta hai.
- **B:** B positive thinking impose karke concern explore nahi karta.
- **C:** C generalization patient ke individual experience ko minimize karti hai.
- **D:** D family ki judgment ko patient ke own feelings se upar rakhta hai.

**Exam clue:** Reflect feeling first, then explore concern.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK610828/table/ptii.tab1/)

</details>

## Q2 — key D

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Focusing technique scattered conversation ko patient ki identified priority par gently organize karti hai. Nurse pehle concerns sun sakti hai, phir pooch sakti hai ki abhi kaunsi baat sabse important lag rahi hai. Isse patient ko control milta hai aur limited time mein meaningful assessment ho sakti hai. Urgent clinical safety concern ho toh usko timely address karna hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A interruption aur diagnostic list patient ki priority clear nahi karti.
- **B:** B topic change karne se actual concern unaddressed rehta hai.
- **C:** C nurse ki selected priority impose karta hai.
- **D:** D patient-identified concern par focused exploration karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Focusing is collaborative, not controlling.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK610828/table/ptii.tab1/)

</details>

## Q3 — key C

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Offering self ka matlab professional capacity mein apna time aur attentive presence offer karna hai. Patient worried hai, nurse uske saath baithne aur concern discuss karne ka realistic offer de sakti hai. Ismein medical outcome guarantee nahi hota. Jo time promise kiya hai usko fulfill karo ya appropriate follow-up arrange karo.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A worry ko unjustified bata kar feeling reject karta hai.
- **B:** B exact personal experience jaanne ka unsupported claim karta hai.
- **C:** C available time aur presence offer karta hai.
- **D:** D uncertain outcome ka guarantee false reassurance hai.

**Exam clue:** Offer presence, not promises.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK610828/table/ptii.tab1/)

</details>

## Q4 — key B

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Reflecting feelings mein nurse patient ki expressed ya apparent emotion ko tentative language mein acknowledge karti hai. Treatment overwhelming lag raha hai, toh managing tasks ke concern ko reflect karna patient ko feeling clarify karne ka chance deta hai. Nurse check kare ki interpretation sahi hai, emotion ko fact ki tarah impose na kare.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A subject change nahi hua, response same concern par hai.
- **B:** B emotional concern reflect hua hai.
- **C:** C patient ko task perform karne ka directive nahi diya gaya.
- **D:** D disease ka diagnosis nahi kiya gaya.

**Exam clue:** Reflecting feelings names emotion, paraphrasing restates meaning.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK610828/table/ptii.tab1/)

</details>

## Q5 — key D

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Summarizing mein interview ke main points aur agreed actions concise form mein review kiye jaate hain. Patient details correct kar sakta hai aur nurse confirm kar sakti hai ki dono same plan samajh rahe hain. Agar koi pending concern hai toh uska follow-up specify karo. Relevant clinical documentation separately complete karni hoti hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A unrelated topic summary ka purpose nahi hai.
- **B:** B verbal review formal clinical record replace nahi karta.
- **C:** C correction rokna shared understanding ke opposite hai.
- **D:** D main concerns aur next steps review karke understanding confirm karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Summary closes the conversation, not the documentation.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK610828/table/ptii.tab1/)

</details>

## Q6 — key C

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Patient ka fear unlikely hone ke bawajood genuine distress create kar sakta hai. Nurse emotion validate kare, accurate known information simple words mein explain kare aur uncertainty honestly acknowledge kare. Patient ko realistic safety steps bata sakti hai. Agar fear clinical deterioration ya self-harm risk se linked ho toh appropriate assessment aur escalation kare.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A concern avoid karne se fear aur uncertainty unresolved rehte hain.
- **B:** B feared outcome certain kehna evidence ke bina anxiety badha sakta hai.
- **C:** C emotion respect karta hai aur truthful information deta hai.
- **D:** D impossible hone ka promise unsupported hai.

**Exam clue:** Validate emotion without validating an unsupported prediction.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK610828/table/ptii.tab1/)

</details>

## Q7 — key B

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Complex treatment decision mein accurate language access informed participation ke liye essential hai. Qualified interpreter patient ki preferred language mein material benefits, risks aur alternatives convey karne mein help karta hai. Nurse directly patient se baat kare, short segments use kare aur understanding verify kare. Consent process authorized clinician aur facility policy ke according complete hota hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A gestures complex risks accurately explain nahi kar sakte.
- **B:** B trained interpretation aur direct patient engagement support karta hai.
- **C:** C child par emotional burden aur accuracy/privacy risk ho sakta hai.
- **D:** D patient ko conversation se exclude karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Speak to the patient, not only to the interpreter.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK599382/?report=printable)

</details>

## Q8 — key A

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Interpreter ko long technical paragraph dene se memory aur translation burden badhta hai. Nurse ek idea at a time plain language mein explain kare, interpretation ke liye pause kare aur patient ko question poochne de. Important medical terms ka meaning explain karo, material information omit mat karo. Understanding teach-back se check ki ja sakti hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A short clear segments aur clarification support karta hai.
- **B:** B speed badhane se message miss ho sakta hai.
- **C:** C difficult concepts omit karne se informed decision compromise ho sakta hai.
- **D:** D unfamiliar abbreviations extra confusion create karti hain.

**Exam clue:** Chunk, pause, interpret, verify.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK599382/?report=printable)

</details>

## Q9 — key C

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Low vision ka degree aur patient ki preferred format vary kar sakti hai. Nurse pooche ki large print, audio, tactile explanation ya guided demonstration mein kya helpful hai. Device ko safely orient karo aur patient ko appropriate assistance ke saath return demonstration ka chance do. Family involvement patient ki consent aur preference ke according ho.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A vision impairment se independent learning ability automatically eliminate nahi hoti.
- **B:** B loudness visual access improve nahi karti.
- **C:** C accessibility aur practical learning dono address karta hai.
- **D:** D small print sole method barrier ko maintain karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Adapt format to patient, not patient to format.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK599382/?report=printable)

</details>

## Q10 — key B

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Airway device speech ko temporarily limit kar sakta hai without impairing decision-making capacity. Nurse suitable writing board, picture board, gesture system ya communication device arrange kare. Patient ke intended message ko confirm kare, especially yes/no signals. New respiratory distress ho toh urgent assessment first. Patient ki own choices preserve karo.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A communication delay se pain, needs ya distress miss ho sakte hain.
- **B:** B alternative communication aur message validation provide karta hai.
- **C:** C speech difficulty ko incapacity assume karta hai.
- **D:** D silence informed consent establish nahi karti.

**Exam clue:** Cannot speak does not mean cannot decide.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK599382/?report=printable)

</details>

## Q11 — key A

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Cognitive load ka matlab ek time par information process karne ka mental burden hai. Discharge teaching mein essential safety actions pehle cover karo, phir remaining instructions short meaningful chunks mein do. Patient ko rest aur questions ka time do. Har segment ke baad teach-back ya return demonstration se check karo. Written accessible summary support ho sakti hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A information prioritize aur manageable segments mein teach karta hai.
- **B:** B same overloaded method repeat karta hai.
- **C:** C terminology memorization practical self-care ko unnecessarily delay karti hai.
- **D:** D necessary safety instruction miss kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Chunk and check, not dump and repeat.

[Concept reference](https://www.ahrq.gov/health-literacy/improve/precautions/tool5.html)

</details>

## Q12 — key D

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Yes bolna ya nod karna understanding ka reliable proof nahi hai. Patient politeness, embarrassment ya language barrier ki wajah se agree kar sakta hai. Teach-back mein nurse patient ko next action apne words mein explain karne ko kehti hai. Agar gap ho toh explanation simplify karke dobara check kare. Yeh patient ki examination nahi, teaching effectiveness ka check hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A louder yes/no question same limitation rakhta hai.
- **B:** B second nurse ka same question actual comprehension verify nahi karta.
- **C:** C nod ko understanding ka proof maan kar inaccurate record bana sakta hai.
- **D:** D patient ki own explanation se understanding assess karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Teach-back tests explanation quality, not patient intelligence.

[Concept reference](https://www.ahrq.gov/health-literacy/improve/precautions/tool5.html)

</details>

## Q13 — key B

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Closed-ended question specific information quickly obtain kar sakta hai. Time-critical assessment mein allergy, onset ya breathing difficulty jaise immediate safety facts short targeted questions se mil sakte hain. Clinical situation stabilize hone par broader open-ended assessment continue karo. Urgent support ko interview complete hone tak delay mat karo.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A follow-up assessment ki need automatically remove nahi hoti.
- **B:** B rapid specific safety information obtain karta hai.
- **C:** C all interviews closed questions se karne par broader concerns miss ho sakte hain.
- **D:** D one specific answer complex plan comprehension prove nahi karta.

**Exam clue:** Open questions explore, closed questions pinpoint.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q14 — key A

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Eye contact ka meaning culture, personal comfort, disability aur situation ke according vary kar sakta hai. Brief eye contact ko dishonesty ya noncooperation ka standalone sign mat samjho. Respectful nurse patient ki preference poochti hai, appropriate communication style adapt karti hai aur actual message verify karti hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A preference aur cultural variation respect karta hai.
- **B:** B one cultural norm impose karta hai.
- **C:** C brief eye contact se unsupported judgment document karta hai.
- **D:** D necessary care communication stop karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Interpret nonverbal cues in context, never in isolation.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q15 — key D

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Therapeutic nurse-patient relationship patient goals aur professional responsibilities par based hota hai, personal friendship par nahi. Social meeting ya private access dependency, privacy aur conflict-of-interest concerns create kar sakte hain. Nurse respectfully boundary explain kare aur follow-up clinic, helpline ya other approved support resources offer kare. Specific boundary policy follow karo.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A personal relationship professional role blur kar sakti hai.
- **B:** B abrupt unexplained withdrawal patient ko distress kar sakta hai.
- **C:** C personal contact sharing unauthorized care pathway create kar sakti hai.
- **D:** D clear boundary ke saath appropriate support maintain karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Boundaries protect both patient and therapeutic relationship.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q16 — key C

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Orientation phase first therapeutic encounter mein trust aur working agreement establish karne ka stage hai. Nurse role introduce kare, interaction ka purpose aur expected plan discuss kare, patient ki concerns identify kare aur confidentiality ke relevant limits explain kare. Goals jointly develop ho sakte hain. Personal friendship ya absolute secrecy promise professional relationship ka part nahi hai.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A social friendship professional orientation ka goal nahi hai.
- **B:** B lawful safety/reporting exceptions ko ignore karta hai.
- **C:** C role, purpose aur expectations establish karta hai.
- **D:** D final outcome evaluation termination se zyada related hai.

**Exam clue:** Orientation = introduction, trust, purpose and goals.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q17 — key A

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Working phase mein nurse aur patient agreed goals par active work karte hain. Concerns explore karna, coping skills practice karna, treatment-related education aur progress evaluate karna examples hain. Patient ki preferences aur ability ke according strategy modify hoti hai. Nurse supportive guide hai, patient ki decisions automatically replace nahi karti.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A collaborative goal-directed work describe karta hai.
- **B:** B first introduction orientation phase ka activity hai.
- **C:** C closure without current goals address karna working phase nahi hai.
- **D:** D patient involvement remove karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Working = active therapeutic work and coping practice.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q18 — key D

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Termination phase planned professional relationship ke ending ko prepare aur manage karti hai. Nurse progress review kare, unresolved concerns discuss kare aur discharge ke baad follow-up ya support resources clarify kare. Ending contact ke feelings acknowledge karo without indefinite personal relationship create kiye. Receiving team ko relevant care information securely transfer karo.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A indefinite informal contact boundary compromise karta hai.
- **B:** B last-minute disclosure preparation aur continuity reduce kar sakta hai.
- **C:** C inpatient discharge ongoing needs absent hone ka proof nahi hai.
- **D:** D progress, emotions aur continuity sab address karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Termination = review, closure, continuity.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q19 — key C

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Shared decision-making mein patient ke goals, preferences aur informed choice central hote hain. Nurse reasonable options ke relevant benefits, risks aur practical implications explain ya clarify karne mein help kare. Prescriber ya responsible clinician ko scope ke according involve kare. Patient ko apni priorities identify karne ka chance do without nurse ke personal preference impose kiye.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A family automatically decision-maker nahi ban jaati.
- **B:** B appropriate information aur support withhold karta hai.
- **C:** C options aur patient values discuss karta hai.
- **D:** D nurse ki personal choice patient preference replace karti hai.

**Exam clue:** Support decisions, do not make them for capable patients.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q20 — key B

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Repeated video disruption se important message incomplete reh sakta hai. Nurse interruption acknowledge kare, patient ki immediate safety assess kare aur secure accessible alternative arrange kare, jaise approved phone ya rescheduled clinical contact when appropriate. Important information dobara verify karo aur actual communication limitations document karo. Urgent symptoms mein appropriate local emergency pathway use karo.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A full understanding bina check record karna inaccurate hai.
- **B:** B communication barrier aur privacy dono address karta hai.
- **C:** C connection hona complete message delivery prove nahi karta.
- **D:** D public messaging service confidentiality risk create kar sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** A connected call is not proof of a completed consultation.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>

## Q21 — key D

<details><summary>Proposed detailed Hinglish explanation</summary>

Sensitive answers visitors ki presence se change ho sakte hain because patient embarrassed, pressured ya unsafe feel kar sakta hai. Nurse routine private conversation offer kare, confidentiality limits explain kare aur patient ko safely discuss karne ka chance de. Agar abuse ya coercion ka concern emerge ho toh safeguarding policy aur urgent safety needs follow karo. Visitors se confrontation ya unsupported accusation avoid karo.

**Option-by-option reasoning**

- **A:** A sensitive information publicly expose karta hai.
- **B:** B intentional deception assume karta hai without assessment.
- **C:** C visitors ki account patient ki confidential perspective replace nahi kar sakti.
- **D:** D privacy aur safety-sensitive assessment support karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Changing answers can be a context cue, not proof of dishonesty.

[Concept reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590036/)

</details>
